summary: The note argues that impact measurement is essential for social ventures, especially SMEs, to track progress, attract investors and grants, and build credibility. It illustrates the practice with six example enterprises covering goal-setting, standardization, technology, storytelling and resource constraints. It closes by stressing continuous improvement and the strategic, funding and reputational benefits of rigorous measurement.
one_line: Social enterprise SMEs use impact measurement through clear goals, standard metrics, technology, storytelling and continuous improvement to gain funding, trust and better decisions.
key_facts: GreenPath Food was founded in October 2023 by Jack Miller and Ayesha Khan to improve farmers' livelihoods in developing countries and promote sustainable agriculture.
GreenPath Food tracks the number of partner farmers, increases in farmers' incomes, and reductions in carbon emissions; Jack Miller says partnering has, on average, doubled farmers' income.
EduBright was launched in November 2023 by Sarita Deshpande and Liam Neeson (not the actor) to bring innovative educational tools to underprivileged areas.
EduBright set SMART objectives (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound): students reached, improvement in students' grades, and teacher satisfaction with teaching aids.
The key lesson from EduBright is to start with the end in mind: clarity about desired impact guides what should be measured.

CraftLocal, founded in December 2023 by Rita Thompson and Carlos Mendez, connects local artisans with global markets and aligned its metrics with SROI and the Global Impact Investing Network's IRIS metrics.
Standardized metrics eased CraftLocal's communication with stakeholders and allowed comparison with peers.
HealthNet, established in January 2024 by Rebecca Kuo and Marcus Davidson, uses mobile clinics for remote areas and built a custom app tracking health metrics and patient satisfaction.
HealthNet's app analyzes trends and generates reports, enabling real-time resource allocation decisions and demonstrating impact to donors.

Farm-to-Table, founded in February 2024 by chefs Emily Wei and Javier Gomez, links local farmers with urban restaurants and publishes annual impact reports combining statistics with individual stories.
ReThink Plastic, started in March 2024 by Lisa Chung and Mohammed Al-Sayed, faces resource constraints and uses basic digital tools plus occasional third-party evaluations.

The note says impact measurement is a continuous-improvement journey 'without a final destination', and benefits include better strategic decisions, increased funding, enhanced reputation and customer loyalty.
